text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Guntis Ulmanis is going to visit Turkey from Februaru 18 until February 21. His Turkish counterpart, Suleiman Demirel, is due for a visit to Riga in mid-June.
- The head of the Securities Commission, Viktors Gustsons, says that Latvia is catching the eye of big foreign investors.
- The Government of Switzerland has allocated 10.8 million Swiss francs to fund several health care projects in Latvia.
- The controling package of shares in the Riga Jewellery Works was sold for 2.7 lats million at an auction on February 15.
- In January Latvia's state revenues increased 8.5 percent compared with the corresponding period in 1996 to 39.701 million lats.
-The Latvian Privatisation Agency has set April 1 as the final date for strategic investors to buy a stake in Latvian Gas. This is the third time that the deadline has been extended.
- Latvian state-run energy company, Latvenergo, which is scheduled for privatisation, forecasts a 5.9 million lats net profit this year.
- The government of Sweden has granted SEK 1 billion to improve urban heating systems in the three Baltic states and North Western Russia.
